status: Scholars and vidvāns are retained by the month, at the top of each range. Each line shows what it is based on.

rates.label: Vidvān (senior scholar)
rates.value: ₹75,000 to ₹1 lakh a month, priced at ₹1 lakh

rates.label: Turning recorded audio into a verse-addressable edition

asks.title: Bring the four core smṛtis into the index
asks.change: Kane's footnotes that quote Manu, Yājñavalkya, Āpastamba and Gautama start showing where their verse stands, on every page of the History of Dharmaśāstra that cites them.

meter.note: The four smṛtis account for up to 850 more.

proof.label: Kane's History of Dharmaśāstra, with 611 footnotes already located

basis: A vidvān for 4 months, choosing the editions and checking every match: ₹4 lakh
1 engineer-month to source, structure and index the four texts: ₹0.6 lakh

asks.title: Index the names of the Harivaṃśa: the Nāma-Kośa pilot
asks.change: The first index of names for any Purāṇic text: every person, people and place in the Harivaṃśa, verified by scholars and tied to the verse. It is the pilot for the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas.

meter.unit: Harivaṃśa verses with their names indexed
meter.note: Up to 4,034 headwords. No Purāṇa has such an index today.

proof.label: The Mahābhārata's 13,772 named entities, from Sorensen's index

basis: Five pāṭhaśālā scholars for 9 months, reading every verse for its names: ₹33.75 lakh
A vidvān for 9 months, writing and reviewing the entries: ₹9 lakh
3 engineer-months for the reading tool and review queue: ₹1.8 lakh

asks.title: The Purāṇa Nāma-Kośa: an index of names for all eighteen Mahāpurāṇas
asks.change: Every person, people, dynasty and place across the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas, verified by scholars and tied to the verse, so a scholar can ask where Ambarīṣa appears, or which Purāṇas know a tīrtha, and get an answer. Released one Purāṇa at a time, after the Harivaṃśa pilot above has measured the real cost.

meter.unit: Mahāpurāṇa verses with their names indexed
meter.note: No index of names exists for any of them. About ₹27.22 lakh per 10,000 verses, so a single Purāṇa can be sponsored on its own.

proof.label: The Mahābhārata's 13,772 named entities, from Sorensen's index

basis: 27 pāṭhaśālā scholars for 3 years, at the pilot's pace: ₹7.29 crore
6 vidvāns for 3 years, writing and reviewing entries, one to every five readers as in the pilot: ₹2.16 crore
Half an engineer for 3 years to run the reading tool and publish each Purāṇa: ₹10.8 lakh
This is an upper figure. It assumes no saving over the pilot, though the proposal expects reading to get cheaper text by text.

asks.title: Commission a Purāṇa recitation that is addressable from the first day
asks.change: A senior upanyāsakar records a Purāṇa so that every verse can be played at its own address. We begin with one adhyāya to prove the method, then a 30-hour series.

meter.unit: Purāṇa verses you can hear at their own address
meter.note: About 4,000 more, if the series does what the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa's 14 recordings did.

proof.label: Kārtika Māhātmya, 1,094 verses already on the clock

basis: Honorarium, 30 hours at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹1.5 lakh (the trust sets this figure)
Recording, 30 hours at ₹2,000 an hour: ₹0.6 lakh
Turning it into a verse-addressable edition, 30 hours at ₹49: ₹1,470 (measured)
A vidvān for 1 month, checking every verse by ear: ₹1 lakh

asks.title: Record the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka, with the text following the chant
asks.change: The Brāhmaṇa and the Āraṇyaka are already on the Yajurveda site with their svaras, but no one can hear them there. Vidvāns record both, and every word is aligned to the recording, as the Saṃhitā's are, so the text follows the chant.

meter.unit: hours of Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda chant with the text following word by word
meter.note: About 59 hours: 43 for the Brāhmaṇa and 16 for the Āraṇyaka. This is estimated from the length of their text against the Saṃhitā's, and the recording will measure it.

proof.label: The Saṃhitā today: the text follows the chant word by word (beta)

basis: Honorarium for the vidvāns, about 59 hours at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹2.95 lakh (the trust sets this figure)
Recording, about 59 hours at ₹2,000 an hour: ₹1.18 lakh
A vidvān for 2 months, checking the alignment by ear: ₹2 lakh
1 engineer-month to align every word to the recording and publish it: ₹0.6 lakh
The text with svaras is already prepared, so nothing is charged for it.

asks.title: Publish one out-of-print smṛti commentary
asks.change: A rare printed commentary is transcribed, indexed by its own contents, cross-linked to Kane and the index, and published free. Priced per thousand printed pages.

meter.note: The Smṛtimuktāphalam's seven volumes are the precedent. They are online in beta, still being proofread.

proof.label: The Smṛtimuktāphalam, seven volumes, Sanskrit with Tamil

basis: OCR of 1,000 pages, Sanskrit with a regional language: ₹5,000
A junior scholar for 5 months, proofreading about 200 pages a month: ₹3.75 lakh
A vidvān for 1 month, reviewing the proofread text: ₹1 lakh
1 engineer-month to index, cross-link and publish: ₹0.6 lakh

asks.title: Clean up and publish the Yajurveda bhāṣyas
asks.change: Sāyaṇa's and Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara's commentaries on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā are beside the text for kāṇḍas 1 to 3 only. For kāṇḍas 4 to 7 they exist as typed files with gaps, and Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara on the Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka exists only as scanned pages. Each is proofread, checked by a scholar, tied to its anuvāka and published beside the text.

meter.unit: Saṃhitā anuvākas with both bhāṣyas beside the text
meter.note: Then Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara on the Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka: 2,611 scanned pages, none on the site yet.

proof.label: Both bhāṣyas beside the Saṃhitā, kāṇḍas 1 to 3 (beta)

basis: OCR of 2,611 scanned pages of Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: ₹0.13 lakh
Two junior scholars for 8 months, proofreading about 3,200 pages at 200 pages a month each: ₹12 lakh. A source for Sāyaṇa on kāṇḍas 5 and 7 still has to be found.
A vidvān for 9 months, reviewing both bhāṣyas: ₹9 lakh
3 engineer-months to structure each bhāṣya by anuvāka, tie it to the text and publish: ₹1.8 lakh

asks.title: Vedic Abhyāsa: a chanting tutor for pāṭhaśālās
asks.change: Śrī Rudram and Chamakam in all four pāṭhas, with the app telling a student which svaras went high or low against the ācārya. Released on Android and iPhone and piloted in pāṭhaśālās across three states.

meter.note: First it must pass our planted-error test: catch known mistakes in a recorded line.

proof.label: Svarānugamī on the Yajurveda: the text follows the chant word by word

basis: 1 engineer for 12 months: ₹7.2 lakh
The ācārya's recordings of saṃhitā, krama and jaṭā: ₹2 lakh
Pilot coordination and devices for pāṭhaśālās: ₹5 lakh

program.title: Or carry the team for a year
program.change: Vidvāns, junior scholars, engineering and hosting for twelve months, spent on the results above in the order the trust sets, so the work does not wait for each line to be funded.
basis: A vidvān for 12 months, across the projects: ₹12 lakh
Two junior scholars for 12 months, across the projects: ₹18 lakh
2 engineers for 12 months: ₹14.4 lakh
Hosting and audio storage: ₹2 lakh
